qs.q: An infant presents with macrocephaly and symptoms of increased intracranial pressure. Neuroimaging reveals an intraventricular papillary neoplasm in the lateral ventricles. Which tumor is most likely?
qs.e: Choroid plexus tumors are the most frequent CNS tumor in infants under 1 year of age, occurring predominantly supratentorially in the lateral ventricles. They typically present with signs of increased intracranial pressure and macrocephaly in infants.

qs.q: During a neuroendoscopic procedure for refractory infant hydrocephalus, the surgeon targets the lateral ventricles. What is the primary physiological purpose of choroid plexus cauterization during this intervention?
o: To enhance the passive reabsorption across arachnoid villi
To reduce the overall rate of cerebrospinal fluid production
To eradicate infectious organisms from the subarachnoid space
To permanently close the communication between ventricles
qs.e: Choroid plexus cauterization aims to reduce the rate of cerebrospinal fluid production by the choroid plexus to help control pressure. It is often combined with an Endoscopic Third Ventriculostomy to improve surgical success.

qs.q: An infant with developmental delay undergoes a brain MRI that demonstrates widely spaced lateral ventricles with concave medial borders, resembling the shape of a bat wing, along with parallel configuration of the white matter tracts. Which diagnosis is most likely?
qs.e: Agenesis of the corpus callosum leads to uncrossed white matter tracts known as Probst bundles, which physically separate the lateral ventricles and give them a bat-wing appearance. Dandy-Walker malformation involves cerebellar vermis hypoplasia and an enlarged posterior fossa cyst.

qs.q: Following its production by the choroid plexus in the lateral ventricles, cerebrospinal fluid travels through a specific interventricular conduit to reach the third ventricle. What is this foramen called?
qs.e: CSF flows from the lateral ventricles through the interventricular foramina of Monro to the third ventricle. The cerebral aqueduct then carries it from the third to the fourth ventricle.

qs.q: A 19-year-old primigravida notes minimal fetal movement at 17 weeks gestation. The maternal serum alpha-fetoprotein is not increased. Fetal ultrasound shows enlargement of lateral ventricles of the brain. Which of the following abnormalities is the most likely cause?
qs.e: Aqueductal stenosis prevents passage of cerebrospinal fluid from the lateral ventricles and third ventricle to the fourth ventricle, leading to an obstructive, non-communicating hydrocephalus. Since the AFP is not elevated, there is no open defect.

qs.q: A 32-year-old man has 2 months of worsening headaches. No lymphadenopathy or organomegaly. CBC: Hgb 12, platelets 250,000, WBC 6000 with 80% granulocytes and 10% lymphocytes. Head CT shows a 3 cm mass next to the right lateral ventricle. Biopsy shows diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. Most likely lab finding?
qs.e: Primary CNS diffuse large B-cell lymphoma in a 32-year-old with relative lymphopenia = AIDS-related lymphoma. HIV infection is the most important risk factor. HIV-1 RNA viral load would be detectable, reflecting underlying HIV infection driving the lymphoma.
